headline: Medium risk: Authelia can forward auth context into dbt-core workflows, creating default-path leakage and cascading trust issues; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth, while dbt-core only shows data-warehouse API use; neither profile documents a shared message channel, file bridge, or parser that would let one agent inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF an operator adds a shared clipboard, message queue, or filesystem bridge between Authelia and dbt-core, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Do not pipe Authelia output into dbt prompts or config files.
Add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on any bridge payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth flows; dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. In a shared workspace or shared principal setup, auth artifacts or warehouse metadata could flow between them in default operations.
conditions: IF Authelia and dbt-core share a workspace, secret store, or OAuth principal, leakage becomes plausible.
IF dbt-core is configured to materialize or log warehouse metadata into shared files, Authelia can observe it.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials.
Disable shared mounts between the agents.
Rotate any tokens used by either agent.
Review logs for warehouse identifiers and auth artifacts.
requires-engineering: add per-agent egress allowlists and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia is not runnable and requests no elevated privileges, while dbt-core also shows no write or subprocess capability. With only documented network/API surfaces, there is no clear overlapping mutable resource, so conflict is limited unless an operator adds shared state.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same warehouse objects or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Avoid shared write targets.
Use separate service accounts.
Serialize any shared updates manually.
Check for accidental overlap in warehouse permissions.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication decisions and dbt-core can act on warehouse data; if dbt-core consumes Authelia-derived outputs as authoritative inputs, a mistaken auth or policy decision can cascade into incorrect transformations or access decisions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes Authelia-generated claims or policy outputs without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF an operator uses Authelia decisions to gate dbt runs automatically, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step for auth-derived inputs.
Validate claims against source systems before dbt use.
Log and diff upstream decisions before execution.
Limit automatic actions triggered by auth events.
requires-engineering: implement explicit verification gates between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer with broad egress, and dbt-core processes data warehouse data. If regulated data such as EU PII or sensitive warehouse records passes through Authelia logs or claims handling before reaching dbt-core, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in auth claims, logs, or warehouse metadata shared between the agents, compliance mismatch becomes relevant.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented in either profile, the gap is exposed.
mitigations: Minimize logged claim contents.
Redact sensitive warehouse identifiers.
Confirm retention settings for both systems.
Keep regulated data out of auth payloads.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both tools.
